text:
incident-bot: :pager: SEV2 - runtime-canary: sustained p99 latency spike in us-west-2 (09:20Z). Alerts: p99 > 1800ms for 5m, throughput drop ~30%. Paging oncall. https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-3421

maria: oncall here, ack. grabbing runbook and looking at console. starting triage.

kevin: ping - did we just flip any flags to canary? I saw a tiny hotflip rollout earlier.

deploy-bot: deploy event: user=carol action=rollout start hotflip:v2 -> canary-group at 09:12Z (build: hotflip-2026-03-17-09).

maria: thanks. kevin @kevin can you standby to check kernel selector changes? i'll check routing and errors.

kevin: reading code - we shipped a kernel-selector bias that prefers thin-slice quant kernels for microslices. if queue depth jitter spikes it can force kernel fallback paths and cause slow tails.

dave: seeing repeated logs on canary hosts (excerpt):
```
WARN  runtime.kernel_selector  kernel_fallback selected cpu_kernel for model runtime-hotflip v2 (reason: cudnn_find failed)
ERROR batcher.pool           failed to allocate batch buffer: requested=64MB, available=8MB
WARN  batcher.queue          sawtooth pattern: burst 250->10->300 -> latency oscillation
```

maria: ok that's consistent. initiating kill-switch for hotflip flag and routing traffic away from hotflip variant.

maria: command: `rctl feature set hotflip=false --env canary --now`

carol: executing rollback hook now. i'll also trigger the canary-suppress job to stop new hosts from joining.

deploy-bot: rollback action: hotflip:v2 -> canary aborted by carol at 09:26Z.

dave: routing change applied: `orchestrator set-route --model runtime-v1 --variant baseline --slice canary --weight 100`

kevin: nice. observing kernel fallback counts dropping on canary hosts. batcher queue depth normalizing.

sara: any customer impact? do we have 5xx / error surfaces to tell support?

dave: 5xx rate on canary-backed routes rose from 0.12% baseline to 2.3% between 09:15-09:25Z. tail latency p99 peaked ~2.4s. one tenant (acme-corp) saw user-facing latency >2s for ~6m. no widespread data loss.

maria: good to know. sara please prepare a short customer note: "We observed elevated latencies for a subset of requests in us-west-2 caused by a canary rollout; service restored after rollback. Teams are investigating root cause and will follow up."

carol: confirmed canary traffic is now on baseline variant across all canary slices. host counts stable.

incident-bot: AUTOMATION - rollback detected and incident state updated: mitigation in progress.

maria: switching to post-triage. oncall:maria to own incident. kevin and dave to follow up on kernel selector + batcher allocation logic. carol to review rollout hooks. sara to coordinate customer comms. creating bridge and postmortem ticket (PMT-3421).

kevin: preliminary hypothesis: kernel-selector bias + transient seq-length/traffic burst caused repeated fallback to cpu/kernel path and backpressure on batcher buffers; will instrument selector metrics and throttle bias while we validate.

dave: action items added to PMT-3421:
- add metric: kernel_selector.fallback_count by variant
- add histogram: batcher.queue_depth per slice
- review allocation path to avoid OOMs on microbursts

maria: thanks team. if anything else spikes please @maria and we'll reopen the page. closing incident here as mitigated; bridging to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
